A1.justification: Both complete 14-page PDFs describe the same LCES study. Their text, equations, four figures, ten tables, and Appendices A–E support reliable comparison despite layout changes.

before.justification: v1 reports original LCES evaluations on ASAP and TOEFL11, including baseline comparisons, ablations, inductive evaluation, and appendix results.

after.justification: v2 retains those original experimental results and additionally reports a statistical comparison with two supervised baselines.

M1.justification: The pairwise comparison procedure, position-bias correction, shared-MLP RankNet, loss, and output conversion are unchanged. Figure 3 relabeling and the rewritten inductive-setting explanation do not introduce a different method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same eight prompts in each of ASAP and TOEFL11. Transductive and inductive scenarios already appear in v1; Section 5.4 is clarified without expanding coverage.

E2.justification: The corresponding comparisons retain Vanilla and MTS; NPCR, BERT, RoBERTa, PAES, and PMAES; and Bradley–Terry and Elo. The added significance testing does not introduce another comparator.

E3.justification: Evaluation splits, metrics, LLM configurations, comparison budgets, training settings, and score conversion remain unchanged. The embedding-identifier edits are documentation corrections, with no reported encoder replacement; the statistical addition does not change the evaluation design.

E4.justification: The position-bias ablation, comparison-budget analysis, inductive evaluation, embedding sensitivity, and human-agreement analysis retain the same experimental evidence. No ablation, robustness experiment, error analysis, or case study is added.

E5.justification: Section 5.1 newly reports Wilcoxon signed-rank testing of LCES with Llama-3.1-8B against PAES and PMAES at a 0.05 significance threshold. It adds no run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or exact p-values.

E6.justification: v2 newly reports no statistically significant QWK differences between LCES and either PAES or PMAES, with both p-values above 0.05. Existing numerical entries in all ten tables and the performance curves in Figure 4 are unchanged.

T1.justification: The debiased-label definition, preference probability, cross-entropy objective, and linear score transformation are unchanged. Neither version adds a theorem, proof, or substantive mathematical derivation relative to the other.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction contributions, and conclusion retain the same claims about pairwise zero-shot AES, RankNet efficiency, performance, backbone robustness, and inductive applicability.

C2.justification: Section 4.4 removes the summary assertion of reliable scaling with model size and describes backbone variability more directly. The Limitations section replaces the concrete recommendation to manually score a benchmark subset with general caution about high-stakes exams, reducing the specificity of deployment guidance.

D1.justification: Section 4.3 and Appendix B/Table 7 change the documented identifiers from text-embedding-v3-large/small to text-embedding-3-large/small. Dimensions, scores, and other implementation settings remain unchanged, supporting a naming correction rather than an actual model change.

R1.justification: The cited works and research positioning are retained. Expanded author lists for Grattafiori et al. and Qin et al., and capitalization corrections, update bibliographic metadata without adding research references.

P1.justification: v2 reformats the contributions as a numbered list, rewrites portions of the introduction and inductive-setting explanation, and removes a results-summary paragraph. It also adds a ChatGPT writing-assistance acknowledgment; the overall section structure remains intact.

P2.justification: Figure 3 replaces the MLP labels with Scoring model f and adjusts spacing. Appendix prompt boxes are reformatted, Tables 7–10 move to later pages, and printed page numbers disappear. The four-figure, ten-table inventory and overall two-column layout remain.

improvement.justification: Corrected embedding identifiers, clearer inductive-setting prose, and added statistical reporting provide modest improvements in clarity and reproducibility. Removing the model-size-scaling assertion also improves restraint. The benefits are limited: nonsignificance does not establish equivalence, and replacing concrete manual-validation guidance with generic caution weakens the limitations discussion. The method and existing experimental scores remain unchanged.
